Create exactly one complete Python source file that deploys the Hugging Face model dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-ABLITERATED-NVFP4 on Modal as a publicly reachable, OpenAI-compatible inference service. The output must contain only that Python file’s source code and no surrounding explanation, Markdown fence, documentation, test, example, client, shell, Dockerfile, YAML, TOML, JSON, requirements, or other file.

Before writing code, resolve compatibility from the actual model repository and the selected vLLM release. Do not claim support for a feature merely because a command-line flag exists. Use a vLLM version and CUDA/PyTorch base image that genuinely support this model’s glm5_next architecture, NVFP4 weights, MoE execution, Marlin MoE kernels, multimodal vision inputs, reasoning parsing, tool calling, and any MTP/speculative-decoding mechanism actually supported by that release. If a requested feature is not supported by the selected stable runtime, do not invent an implementation or silently pretend it works; choose a compatible supported runtime or fail clearly during image build/startup. Keep the model’s native quantized weights and vision components intact.

Use the exact model ID:

dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-ABLITERATED-NVFP4

Create one Modal App, one GPU-serving deployment, and all required image, volume, secret, lifecycle, and HTTP declarations in the same file. The file must be deployable with:

modal deploy <python-file>

Do not require a locally running background process after deployment.

Use a four-GPU configuration and genuinely pass tensor parallelism to vLLM:

--tensor-parallel-size 4

Select a Modal GPU class with sufficient VRAM, CUDA capability, and kernel support for the model’s NVFP4/MoE runtime. Make the GPU type, GPU count, tensor-parallel size, image tag, vLLM version, port, cache paths, concurrency, autoscaling limits, context limit, and generation limits explicit top-level configuration values. Do not select a GPU configuration that is unlikely to load the complete model.

Use the model’s required serving options where they are supported by the selected vLLM version:

--moe-backend marlin
--enable-auto-tool-choice
--tool-call-parser glm47
--reasoning-parser glm45

Do not add unsupported flags. Do not implement a fake parser, fake MTP, fake batching layer, fake endpoint, fallback model, dummy completion, or simulated response. If MTP/speculative decoding requires additional model-specific vLLM arguments, configure them only when verified to be valid for this model and installed runtime. Otherwise preserve the model’s MTP head without falsely advertising unsupported speculative decoding.

Build the container with all dependencies required by the chosen vLLM runtime. Pin mutually compatible versions of the CUDA base image, PyTorch, vLLM, transformers, tokenizer/runtime packages, and any multimodal or quantization dependencies. Prefer a stable published vLLM image or a reproducible pinned installation when it provides verified support. Do not use an arbitrary nightly combination. If a source revision is unavoidable, pin the exact repository and commit in the single Python file and make the build fail visibly if installation fails.

Use persistent Modal Volumes for the Hugging Face cache and vLLM compilation/cache artifacts. Mount them at explicit paths and set the corresponding environment variables before model loading, including HF_HOME, HF_HUB_CACHE, TRANSFORMERS_CACHE where applicable, and vLLM/PyTorch compilation cache paths. Configure the image and runtime so the model is downloaded once into persistent storage rather than on every restart. Enable HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER=1 only when the installed environment supports it. Do not assume that a Volume can be created automatically at runtime if Modal requires declaration-time creation; define the volumes using the correct Modal API and make deployment fail clearly if creation or mounting is invalid.

Support optional Hugging Face authentication without embedding credentials. Accept a token through a Modal Secret or environment variable, and pass it to the container only when present. Never hardcode a token. Do not make public-model access depend on a token unnecessarily.

Start one real vLLM OpenAI-compatible server inside the GPU container. Bind it to 0.0.0.0 on an explicit internal port. Load the model once during container startup, not once per request. Use the vLLM OpenAI server’s native HTTP implementation rather than reimplementing generation. Expose the server through Modal’s supported public HTTP mechanism, using the current Modal API syntax for the selected runtime. The public endpoint must be usable by an external application with an OpenAI-compatible base URL ending in /v1.

The service must expose at least:

GET /v1/models
POST /v1/chat/completions

Use vLLM’s native OpenAI-compatible routes so that request validation, response schemas, streaming, tool calls, multimodal content, and usage metadata are handled by the actual serving engine. Support model name, messages, temperature, top-p, maximum output tokens, stop sequences, presence penalty, frequency penalty, stream mode, tools, tool choice, multimodal message content, and model-supported reasoning parameters. Do not wrap the API in a simplified /generate endpoint. Do not fabricate /v1/models; it must reflect the loaded model and serving configuration.

Streaming must be genuine server-sent event streaming produced while tokens are generated. Do not generate a complete response first and split it afterward. Ensure the Modal HTTP proxy preserves streaming behavior and does not buffer the entire response.

Use the native tokenizer and chat template from the model repository and vLLM. Do not replace or rewrite the template. Preserve text, reasoning, tool-calling, and vision behavior supported by the model. Forward OpenAI-compatible multimodal message content in the format accepted by the selected vLLM release. Do not disable the vision tower. Do not modify model weights at runtime.

Configure realistic memory and context settings. The model may declare a context capacity up to 1M tokens, but do not set a 1M-token runtime context by default if it makes KV-cache allocation, latency, or cost impractical. Define a production-usable maximum model length explicitly, document it only through variable names or code configuration, and ensure it is accepted by the selected vLLM version. Set GPU memory utilization below the absolute limit when necessary for runtime headroom. Configure batching, maximum concurrent sequences, and maximum batched tokens explicitly enough to prevent uncontrolled memory growth. Use vLLM’s native continuous/in-flight batching rather than a custom queue.

Configure Modal concurrency and autoscaling conservatively for a four-GPU replica. Do not create multiple four-GPU replicas by default unless the configuration explicitly limits them. Set a sensible minimum and maximum container count, request concurrency, startup timeout, idle timeout, and scaledown behavior for a large model. Ensure the Modal concurrency settings do not cause multiple independent vLLM processes to compete for the same GPUs inside one container. Use one vLLM process per four-GPU replica unless the selected runtime explicitly requires another arrangement.

Implement a clear startup/readiness lifecycle. Mount persistent volumes, set environment variables, validate GPU visibility and required runtime versions, launch vLLM, wait for the server’s actual readiness endpoint, and only then accept public traffic. Propagate subprocess failures, timeout failures, invalid arguments, missing GPUs, model download failures, CUDA errors, and incompatible runtime errors to Modal logs and process status. Do not suppress exceptions, return fake health success, or continue after the vLLM process exits. Terminate the child process cleanly when the container shuts down.

Use only APIs and decorators valid for the current Modal SDK. Avoid obsolete or ambiguous patterns. If using a subprocess-based vLLM server, implement robust process supervision, readiness polling, signal handling, stdout/stderr propagation, and cleanup entirely in the same Python file. If using Modal’s native ASGI/FastAPI integration, proxy requests to the local vLLM server without changing OpenAI request or response semantics and preserve streaming responses. Do not introduce an unnecessary custom generation implementation.

Keep all non-secret configuration in explicit constants or environment-backed variables in the file. Keep secrets outside source code. Do not reference any external local file, requirements.txt, Dockerfile, configuration file, or additional source module. Do not use TODO, pass, ellipses, placeholders, pseudocode, mock data, or incomplete branches. Every imported package must be installed or provided by the selected image, and every declared Modal object must be used correctly.

The final source file must include all required imports, Modal App definition, image definition, pinned runtime dependencies, persistent Volume declarations, optional Secret integration, GPU configuration, vLLM arguments, cache environment, startup/readiness supervision, public OpenAI-compatible HTTP exposure, concurrency/autoscaling configuration, and clean shutdown logic. It must load exactly dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-ABLITERATED-NVFP4, use four-way tensor parallelism, use the verified Marlin MoE configuration when supported, enable the verified reasoning and tool-call parsers, preserve multimodal vision support, and use native vLLM support for any MTP capability that is actually available.

Return only the complete Python source code.
Send back the complete code with all the fixes. Fix each of the listed errors one by one, making sure to actually correct them so that there are 0 errors remaining. Keep the original imports, since the files exist. Write out every single character; do not abbreviate anything. Fix every error. There must be exactly one file. Do not write anything else; just output the complete code, and it must not contain any comments. Never, under any circumstances, use simplified, substitute, dummy, simulated, or fake code. Write the entire file as complete, unabridged, production-ready code in a single code block. It must be 100% error-free, a complete, error-free file, and must be submitted as a downloadable file. These requirements are mandatory and must be strictly adhered to. If no list of errors is provided, you must find all the errors and fix them. If there were comments in the original code, delete them. And most importantly: YOU MUST NEVER SIMPLIFY!

```python
import os
import signal
import subprocess
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import modal

MODEL_ID = "dealignai/GLM-5.3-Flash-ABLITERATED-NVFP4"
IMAGE_TAG = "vllm/vllm-openai:glm53-flash-x86_64-cu130"
GPU_TYPE = "B200:4"
GPU_COUNT = 4
TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE = 4
INTERNAL_PORT = 8000
MAX_MODEL_LEN = 32768
GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION = 0.92
MAX_NUM_SEQS = 64
MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS = 32768
MIN_CONTAINERS = 0
MAX_CONTAINERS = 1
CONTAINER_CONCURRENCY = 128
STARTUP_TIMEOUT = 1800
SCALEDOWN_WINDOW = 300
ALLOW_CONCURRENT_INPUTS = 100

HF_HOME_PATH = "/root/cache/huggingface"
VLLM_CACHE_PATH = "/root/cache/vllm"
TORCH_CACHE_PATH = "/root/cache/torch"

hf_cache_volume = modal.Volume.from_name("glm-53-flash-hf-cache", create_if_missing=True)
vllm_cache_volume = modal.Volume.from_name("glm-53-flash-vllm-cache", create_if_missing=True)

app = modal.App(name="glm-5-3-flash-abliterated-nvfp4")

image = (
    modal.Image.from_registry(IMAGE_TAG)
    .pip_install(
        "hf_transfer==0.1.9",
        "huggingface_hub>=0.28.0",
        "fastapi>=0.115.0",
        "httpx>=0.27.0",
        "uvicorn>=0.30.0",
    )
    .env(
        {
            "HF_HOME": HF_HOME_PATH,
            "HF_HUB_CACHE": f"{HF_HOME_PATH}/hub",
            "TRANSFORMERS_CACHE": f"{HF_HOME_PATH}/hub",
            "HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER": "1",
            "VLLM_CACHE_ROOT": VLLM_CACHE_PATH,
            "TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR": TORCH_CACHE_PATH,
            "VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND": "FLASH_ATTN",
        }
    )
)

@app.cls(
    image=image,
    gpu=GPU_TYPE,
    volumes={
        HF_HOME_PATH: hf_cache_volume,
        VLLM_CACHE_PATH: vllm_cache_volume,
    },
    secrets=[modal.Secret.from_name("huggingface-secret", required=False)],
    timeout=STARTUP_TIMEOUT,
    scaledown_window=SCALEDOWN_WINDOW,
    min_containers=MIN_CONTAINERS,
    max_containers=MAX_CONTAINERS,
    allow_concurrent_inputs=ALLOW_CONCURRENT_INPUTS,
)
class VLLMServer:
    @modal.enter()
    def start_server(self):
        os.environ["HF_HOME"] = HF_HOME_PATH
        os.environ["HF_HUB_CACHE"] = f"{HF_HOME_PATH}/hub"
        os.environ["TRANSFORMERS_CACHE"] = f"{HF_HOME_PATH}/hub"
        os.environ["HF_HUB_ENABLE_HF_TRANSFER"] = "1"
        os.environ["VLLM_CACHE_ROOT"] = VLLM_CACHE_PATH
        os.environ["TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR"] = TORCH_CACHE_PATH
        os.environ["VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND"] = "FLASH_ATTN"

        cmd = [
            "python3",
            "-m",
            "vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server",
            "--model",
            MODEL_ID,
            "--served-model-name",
            MODEL_ID,
            "--tensor-parallel-size",
            str(TENSOR_PARALLEL_SIZE),
            "--host",
            "0.0.0.0",
            "--port",
            str(INTERNAL_PORT),
            "--moe-backend",
            "marlin",
            "--enable-auto-tool-choice",
            "--tool-call-parser",
            "glm47",
            "--reasoning-parser",
            "glm45",
            "--gpu-memory-utilization",
            str(GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION),
            "--max-model-len",
            str(MAX_MODEL_LEN),
            "--max-num-seqs",
            str(MAX_NUM_SEQS),
            "--max-num-batched-tokens",
            str(MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS),
            "--trust-remote-code",
        ]

        self.process = subprocess.Popen(
            cmd,
            stdout=None,
            stderr=None,
        )

        health_url = f""
        start_time = time.time()
        ready = False

        while time.time() - start_time < STARTUP_TIMEOUT:
            retcode = self.process.poll()
            if retcode is not None:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"vLLM server exited prematurely with return code {retcode}"
                )
            try:
                req = urllib.request.Request(health_url)
                with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=2) as resp:
                    if resp.status == 200:
                        ready = True
                        break
            except Exception:
                pass
            time.sleep(2)

        if not ready:
            self.process.kill()
            raise TimeoutError("Timed out waiting for vLLM server to become ready")

    @modal.exit()
    def stop_server(self):
        if hasattr(self, "process") and self.process is not None:
            if self.process.poll() is None:
                self.process.terminate()
                try:
                    self.process.wait(timeout=30)
                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                    self.process.kill()
                    self.process.wait()

    @modal.web_server(port=INTERNAL_PORT, startup_timeout=STARTUP_TIMEOUT)
    def serve(self):
        pass
```
